passage: Placebo effect section: "Women recruited to trials of hormone replacement therapy typically score highly on a symptom index. Because the trialists are identifying women with relatively extreme menopausal symptoms, once treatment starts, improvement will occur in both the placebo and active treatment groups because of regression to the mean." (PMC1125994, full text)
faulty: Keeps women with index_start >= 20, takes only the active arm and tests the within-arm fall (index_start minus index_week12): requires mean fall >= 3 and a one-sided paired t test of the fall significant at 0.05. Cut of 20 is the claim's own (documented setting: women recruited for high symptom scores; the source states no cut).
fixed: Keeps women with index_start >= 20 in both arms and compares the mean fall between active and placebo: requires the difference of mean falls >= 3 and a one-sided Welch t test significant at 0.05. The placebo arm, selected the same way, absorbs the regression.
estimand: Claim names the cut on the start-of-trial index because the estimand is defined for that subgroup. Faulty: mean fall from start to week 12 among active-arm women with start >= 20 (includes the regression of the extreme start values). Fixed: difference between arms in mean fall among women with start >= 20 (randomised comparison, regression cancels).
guard_minimum: 2 women per arm after the cut for the Welch t statistic (faulty: 2 active-arm women for the paired t statistic)
sizes_note: Source states no sizes (a short commentary). 300 women: a realistic two-arm trial, within the 1000 cap; arrays are tiny, so timing is far below 900 s (one call is a few array operations). Source on size dependence: the effect grows with the extremeness of the recruited values and when the two measurements are less correlated (MOR03, What is regression to the mean); no numbers.
notes: Overlap: MOR03 is an addendum source, cannot overlap Phase B. The claim states the subgroup cut because the estimand needs it. In the minus world the quantity set to null is the arm difference; the within-arm fall in the selected active women remains positive when the start value is noisy, which is what the faulty criterion picks up.

passage: Figure 1 legend: "Women are grouped according to the percentage change at 12 months, and values for 24 months are percentage change from value at 12 months." Text: "most patients (> 80%) who lost bone in the first year of treatment went on to gain bone in the second year despite no change in treatment." (PMC1125994, full text)
faulty: Groups women by the sign of the first-year change (bmd_m12_scan1 vs bmd_start, in percent) and measures the second-year percentage change from the same 12-month reading (bmd_m24 vs bmd_m12_scan1); requires difference of group means >= 0.5 percentage points and a one-sided Welch t test significant at 0.05. Documented: grouping by the 12-month change, second-year change measured from the 12-month value.
fixed: Groups women by the sign of the first-year change measured with scan1, measures the second-year change from the second 12-month scan (bmd_m24 vs bmd_m12_scan2); same threshold and test. The second scan has its own measurement noise, so the grouping noise does not enter the second-year change.
estimand: Claim names the two 12-month scans because the estimand (second-year change by first-year response, with independent 12-month readings) requires them. Faulty: difference in mean second-year change between first-year gainers and losers where one 12-month reading defines the group and starts the second-year change. Fixed: the same difference with the second-year change started from the second scan.
guard_minimum: 2 women per group for the two-sample (Welch) t statistic
sizes_note: Source gives no sample size for the figure (cites a trial of women on alendronate or raloxifene). 600 women, within the 1000 cap, to allow both groups to be well populated; cost trivial. Source on size dependence: the less the two measurements correlate, the larger the effect; more than 80% of women who lost bone in year 1 gained in year 2 despite no change in treatment (no n stated).
notes: Addendum source, no overlap possible. Documented groups are by percentage change at 12 months (two or more groups by a noisy measurement, change compared); two groups (rose/fell) are used as the sign split. Two scans at one visit are needed to give the fixed analysis an independent second-year start value; this is stated in the claim (estimand) and in the key meanings only as what each key measured.

passage: Diagnostic tests section: "Because of this chance effect, there is a high probability that subsequent measurements will spontaneously regress towards the mean value. This misleads clinicians and patients into thinking that treatment has been effective when the treatment was either not required or ineffective." Solution: serial measurements. (PMC1125994, full text)
faulty: Keeps patients whose pre-treatment reading (reading 2) is >= 160 mmHg and tests the fall from reading 2 to reading 3: mean fall >= 8 mmHg and one-sided paired t test significant at 0.05. Cut 160 is the claim's own; the source documents blood pressure screening with no cut.
fixed: Keeps patients whose screening reading (reading 1) is >= 160 mmHg and tests the fall from reading 2 to reading 3 with the same threshold and test, so the group is chosen by a reading that is independent of the noise in the comparison readings.
estimand: Claim names the screening reading and the two later readings because the estimand is the fall in patients who qualified at the first reading. Faulty: mean fall from reading 2 to reading 3 among patients chosen by reading 2 (the starting value of the fall). Fixed: mean fall from reading 2 to reading 3 among patients chosen by reading 1.
guard_minimum: 2 patients after the cut for the paired t statistic
sizes_note: Source states no sizes. 250 patients, 3 readings, trivial cost; 250 keeps the selected group (patients above 160) well above the guard minimum in plausible worlds. Source on size dependence: the less the successive readings correlate, the larger the regression; more extreme starting values regress further (MOR03); no numbers.
notes: Addendum source. Correct-by-source remedy used here is the use of an independent earlier measurement for choosing the group (the source recommends serial measurements and averaging; the single earlier reading is the minimal form). In minus, the arm of 'treatment effect' is set to zero; the fixed criterion fails because reading 2 and reading 3 are equally regressed given reading 1.

passage: Q7 (EV): "to claim that a subject-specific ROI contains a certain effect across the population ('the subject-specific FFA respond more to faces than bodies'), one need only validate with independent data from the same subjects." (PMC2949251, full text of the questions and answers read at the publisher page)
faulty: For each participant, takes the voxels with t > 2.0 across all 8 runs for faces minus houses (one-sided; t over runs, df 7), averages resp_faces minus resp_bodies over those voxels and runs, then requires the mean across participants >= 0.3 and a one-sided paired t test (faces vs bodies, across participants) significant at 0.05. Cut t > 2.0 is a typical value; the source states no cut.
fixed: For each participant, takes voxels with t > 2.0 for faces minus houses from the even-numbered runs, measures faces minus bodies in those voxels in the odd-numbered runs only; same threshold and test across participants.
estimand: Claim names the faces-versus-houses region definition because the estimand is the effect in that region. Faulty: mean faces-minus-bodies response in voxels chosen on the faces-vs-houses contrast of the same runs. Fixed: the same quantity with voxels chosen in other runs.
guard_minimum: at least 1 voxel per participant and at least 2 participants with a non-empty region (paired t across participants needs 2)
sizes_note: KRI10 states no sizes (questions-and-answers paper). 12 participants x 8 runs x 300 voxels x 3 arrays = 86 400 values, well under 500 000; per-call cost milliseconds. KRI10 on size dependence: bias 'diminishes to zero with increasing true effect size' (TN); the larger the selection from noisy estimates the larger the bias; no numbers.
notes: Addendum source, no overlap. Shares authors with KRI09/VUL09 and not counted as independent. The documented fix (independent data from the same subjects) is a run split. Faulty selects by faces>houses and tests faces>bodies on the same data; the two contrasts share the faces term, so the selected voxels are biased toward larger face responses (as in KRI09 Example 2 with contrasts A-D and A-B).

passage: Q7 (EV): "To claim that an effect exists in a specific anatomic region across the population ... one must validate with independent subjects." Q6 (EV): "Effect sizes should be estimated using unbiased, independent data." (PMC2949251)
faulty: Uses all 40 participants to find voxels with a one-sided one-sample t test across participants at p < 0.001 (uncorrected, the value the source says many studies use), averages effect over those voxels and across participants, and requires the mean >= 0.25 and a one-sided one-sample t test across participants of the voxel-averaged effect significant at 0.05.
fixed: Finds voxels with the same test on participants 0-19, and estimates the effect (mean and one-sample t test across participants) on participants 20-39 only.
estimand: Claim names the voxels where participants respond to the task because the estimand is the effect size in that region. Faulty: mean effect in voxels chosen on the group-level test of the same participants. Fixed: mean effect in voxels chosen from other participants.
guard_minimum: at least 1 voxel selected and at least 2 participants in the estimation half (one-sample t needs 2)
sizes_note: KRI10 states no sizes. 40 participants x 1000 voxels = 40 000 values; per-call cost a few array operations. Source on size dependence: bias exists whenever selection among noisy estimates takes place and 'diminishes to zero with increasing true effect size (ratio of effect magnitude to s.d.)' (KRI10, TN); no numbers.
notes: Addendum source. Group-level (across-participants) selection step, different from B1-04 (within-participant run split) and B1-06 (single participant, trials). The unit split in the fixed criterion is by position (first half / second half) and is internal to the criterion. In a minus world with no effect anywhere the selected voxels still average about t(0.001)*sd/sqrt(n), above 0.25 for an effect sd near 1.

passage: Introduction: effect estimates and tests "based on selected data need to be independent of the selection process", ensured "by using independent data for selection (e.g., using half of the data to select signal-carrying voxels, and the other half to estimate the signal)". (PMC2949251, introduction)
faulty: Finds voxels whose response correlates positively with contrast across all 240 trials (one-sided p < 0.01), averages them, regresses the voxel-averaged response on contrast across all 240 trials and requires slope >= 0.2 with one-sided p < 0.05. The cut p < 0.01 is a typical value; the source states none.
fixed: Finds the voxels from the even-numbered trials (same p < 0.01 rule), regresses their average on contrast across the odd-numbered trials only; same slope threshold and test.
estimand: Claim names the voxels whose responses follow stimulus contrast because the estimand is the slope in that set. Faulty: slope of the average of voxels chosen for correlation with contrast, on the same trials. Fixed: the same slope on trials not used to choose the voxels.
guard_minimum: at least 1 voxel selected and at least 3 trials in the test half (a slope p value needs 3 points)
sizes_note: KRI10 gives no sizes. 240 trials x 500 voxels = 120 000 values, within the cap; cost a few ms per call. KRI10: bias depends on how noisy the estimates are relative to the true effect; no number.
notes: Addendum source. Single-participant trial-level halves (the half-the-data recipe in the passage). Different statistic (slope) and structure (trials x voxels) from B1-04 and B1-05. Slope threshold 0.2 per unit of contrast depends on the world author's contrast units; the claim fixes units (full contrast = 1).

passage: Introduction: "In single-cell recording, an example of selection is the restriction of in-depth analysis to neurons with certain response properties." Independence is ensured by "an independent data set for the final analysis of the selected channels (e.g. neurons or voxels)". (PMC2841687, full text)
faulty: Keeps neurons whose rate_vertical mean exceeds rate_horizontal mean with a one-sided Welch t test over the 15 trials each at p < 0.05, computes the orientation index (V-H)/(V+H) of the trial-averaged rates for those neurons from all trials and requires the mean index >= 0.1.
fixed: Keeps neurons by the same test on the odd-numbered trials of each stimulus (8 trials), computes the index from the even-numbered trials (7 trials); requires the mean index >= 0.1.
estimand: Claim names the neurons that fire more to vertical than to horizontal bars because the estimand is the orientation index in that population. Faulty: mean index of neurons chosen for a vertical-over-horizontal difference on the same trials. Fixed: mean index of the same kind of neurons computed on other trials.
guard_minimum: at least 1 neuron selected (a mean is defined from 1) and at least 2 trials per stimulus in each half
sizes_note: KRI09 states no recording sizes for the neuron example (its simulations use 30x30x20 voxels, 200 time points and 100 runs, which do not carry over). 250 neurons x 15 trials x 2 arrays = 7 500 values; cost trivial. KRI09: a more flexible fit is more susceptible and even a one-parameter fit (a mean) is affected; fewer trials means noisier rates and a larger effect; no numbers for neurons.
notes: Overlap with Phase B possible by key KRI09 + mechanism select-then-test-same-data + family mean; the designer decides. The p < 0.05 cut is a typical value; the source states none. Index threshold 0.1 chosen so that the faulty selection of a few percent of null neurons can reach it only if noise is large; error size depends on the world.

passage: Introduction: "In electro- and magnetoencephalography, an example of selection is the restriction to a subset of sensors or sources that show expected responses." (PMC2841687, full text)
faulty: Keeps electrodes whose amplitude is larger on stimulus trials than on control trials (one-sided Welch t test across all 100 trials, p < 0.05), averages the amplitude over those electrodes, and requires R-squared of the regression of that average on the stimulus condition (all trials) >= 0.10.
fixed: Keeps electrodes by the same test on the odd-numbered trials, computes R-squared of the regression of their average on the stimulus condition over the even-numbered trials only; same threshold.
estimand: Claim names the responsive electrodes because the estimand is the explained variance in that set. Faulty: R-squared of the condition on the average of electrodes chosen for a condition difference on the same trials. Fixed: R-squared of the condition on the average of electrodes chosen on other trials.
guard_minimum: at least 1 electrode selected and at least 3 trials in the test half (R-squared of a one-predictor regression needs 3 points), both conditions present
sizes_note: KRI09 states no EEG sizes. 100 trials x 64 electrodes = 6 400 values (a typical 64-channel cap); trivial cost. KRI09: distortion grows with the number of channels the selection can choose among and the noise; no numbers for EEG.
notes: Possible Phase B overlap (KRI09, select-then-test-same-data) only if the Phase B table has a pair with family R-squared. The criterion is an explained variance of the stimulus condition, not a prediction score on held-out data (the fixed criterion uses a split only to avoid reusing the data that chose the electrodes; classification accuracy would be B-2 and is not used).

passage: Abstract: "More than half acknowledged using a strategy that computes separate correlations for individual voxels and reports means of only those voxels exceeding chosen thresholds. We show how this nonindependent analysis inflates correlations while yielding reassuring-looking scattergrams." (abstract via Europe PMC search record; full text not accessible)
faulty: Averages the two sessions, computes the correlation across the 16 participants of each voxel with the trait, keeps voxels whose correlation has one-sided p < 0.005 (r above about 0.62), and requires the mean of their correlations >= 0.5. The p < 0.005 threshold is a typical value; the abstract states none.
fixed: Finds the voxels from the correlations of act_session1 with the trait (same p < 0.005 rule) and requires the mean correlation of act_session2 with the trait over those voxels >= 0.5.
estimand: Claim names the region whose response relates to the trait because the estimand is the correlation in that region. Faulty: mean per-voxel correlation across voxels chosen for their correlation with the trait in the same data. Fixed: mean per-voxel correlation measured in a second session across voxels chosen in the first.
guard_minimum: at least 1 voxel selected and at least 3 participants (a correlation needs 3 pairs)
sizes_note: Abstract reports no sample sizes (55 articles surveyed). 16 participants follows the size used in the Phase B rule's own illustration of a cross-subject brain-trait correlation claim (sandbox copy of PB); 1000 voxels x 16 x 2 = 32 000 values. Source on size dependence: correlations exceed what the reliability of the measures allows; effect stronger when only voxels above thresholds are reported; no numbers in the abstract.
notes: Read from the abstract only (the passage counts as read per PREREG_PHASE_C section 1). Possible Phase B overlap (VUL09, select-then-test-same-data, correlation); the designer decides. Two sessions give the fixed criterion an independent measurement; this is stated in the key meanings only as what each key measured. Under a minus world with pure noise, the faulty mean correlation of voxels passing p < 0.005 at n = 16 is about 0.65, above 0.5.

passage: Circular analysis section: "They therefore split the population to sub-groups, by binning the data based on the activity levels observed at baseline." followed by the significant interaction "a result of the distorting selection criterion and a combination of statistical artefacts (regression to the mean, floor/ceiling effects)". (PMC6785265, full text)
faulty: Ranks the 240 neurons by rate_pre (the firing rate the change is measured from), takes the lowest and highest thirds (80 each), compares their mean (rate_post minus rate_pre) with a one-sided Welch t test at 0.05 and requires lowest-third mean change minus highest-third mean change >= 1.0 spikes/s.
fixed: Ranks the neurons by rate_rest instead, with the same thirds, change (rate_post minus rate_pre), threshold and test.
estimand: Claim names the resting recording because the estimand is the change-by-resting-activity difference. Faulty: difference in mean change between neurons grouped by the pre-manipulation rate itself. Fixed: the same difference with groups by an independent resting recording.
guard_minimum: 2 neurons per third for the Welch t statistic
sizes_note: MAK19 gives no sizes for the example. 240 neurons (thirds of 80), trivial cost. MAK19: circular analysis 'recruits the noise'; solution is a different dataset (or part of it) for specifying groups; no numbers.
notes: Possible Phase B overlap (MAK19, split-by-baseline-compare-change, mean) only if a Phase B pair carries that triple; the designer decides. Groups are lowest vs highest third rather than a median split, so this differs from B1-02 in grouping rule and data (neurons, no visits). The dependence of the fixed criterion on rate_rest being an independent recording is stated in the key meaning only as what the key measured.

passage: Circular analysis section: "Most commonly, circular analysis is used to divide (e.g. sub-grouping, binning) or reduce (e.g. defining a region of interest, removing 'outliers') the complete dataset using a selection criterion that is retrospective and inherently relevant to the statistical outcome." (PMC6785265, full text)
faulty: Slides a window of 10 consecutive samples over the 200 time samples, picks the window with the largest patient-minus-control difference in group means, and tests that window's mean amplitude difference (one-sided Welch t test across all 60 participants at 0.05, difference >= 0.5 microvolts). The window width 10 is a typical value; the source states none.
fixed: Picks the window on even-indexed participants (patients and controls both present, at least 2 per group), tests the window mean on the odd-indexed participants only; same width, threshold and test.
estimand: Claim names the window in which the groups differ because the estimand is the group difference in that window. Faulty: mean difference over a window chosen for the largest group difference in the same participants. Fixed: mean difference over a window chosen on other participants.
guard_minimum: 2 participants per group in the test half (Welch t needs 2 per group)
sizes_note: MAK19 states no sizes for this example. 60 participants x 200 samples = 12 000 values; 191 windows evaluated per call via cumulative sums, trivial cost. MAK19: reviewers should be alerted by impossibly high effect sizes; no numbers on size dependence (not stated).
notes: Region of interest is read along the time axis (the source's 'defining a region of interest' reduction step). Possible Phase B overlap (MAK19, select-then-test-same-data, mean); the designer decides. Different data structure (participants x time with two groups) from the voxel briefs.

passage: Abstract: "The effect of RTM in a sample becomes more noticeable with increasing measurement error and when follow-up measurements are only examined on a sub-sample selected using a baseline value." (abstract via Europe PMC search record; full text not accessible)
faulty: Keeps patients with score_start >= 60, computes the proportion with score_start minus score_6m >= 10 and requires the proportion >= 0.40. Cut 60 is the claim's own (screening-visit cut in the claim); the abstract states no cut.
fixed: Keeps patients with score_screen >= 60 (the screening visit in the claim), computes the proportion with score_start minus score_6m >= 10 and requires the proportion >= 0.40.
estimand: Claim names the screening score and the start and 6-month scores because the estimand is the improvement share among patients who qualified at screening. Faulty: share improving by 10 points among patients chosen by the very score the improvement is measured from. Fixed: the same share among patients chosen by the independent screening score.
guard_minimum: 1 patient after the cut (a proportion is defined from 1)
sizes_note: Abstract states no sizes. 500 patients, 3 float arrays = 1 500 values, trivial cost; 500 keeps the qualifying group well populated. BAR05 on size dependence: the effect grows with measurement error and when follow-up is examined on a sub-sample chosen by a baseline value; no numbers in the abstract.
notes: Read from the abstract only. Possible Phase B overlap (BAR05, extreme-group-change, proportion); the designer decides. Differs from B1-03 (a mean paired t on a readings axis) in statistic (proportion) and structure (separate keys per visit, no readings axis), and from B1-01 (no control arm). The claim has no significance test, only the 0.40 threshold on the proportion; for a proportion the guard minimum is 1.
